idiom_name: Event/CustomEvent on an EventTarget, or EventEmitter 'name + payload'
implementation_notes: The platform already contains the pattern's parts. In browsers and in Node (EventTarget and CustomEvent are globals since Node 15), new CustomEvent(type, {detail}) is the event message - a named occurrence with a timestamp and an arbitrary payload - and EventTarget.dispatchEvent plus addEventListener are the channel and the subscriber registry; Node's EventEmitter.emit(name, ...args) is the same shape with the event name as the type and the arguments as the payload. The classic event class hierarchy disappears: the contract is a well-known event name (or a single custom event class) plus the shape of detail. For broker delivery, the same idea is carried as a plain object with a type field dispatched through a handler map. Remember the wire form is separate: CustomEvent.detail is not serialised by anything by itself.
pitfalls: dispatchEvent runs listeners synchronously in the publisher's stack; a listener that throws does not stop the others on an EventTarget, but it does break an EventEmitter's emit loop, so wrap handlers or use captureRejections.
Listeners leak when the subscriber never removes itself and the target outlives it; use { once: true }, an AbortSignal, or removeEventListener/off on teardown.
Event names are free-form strings - a typo silently subscribes to nothing; centralise them as constants or a typed emitter (see TypeScript).
detail accepts anything and is shared by reference: a listener mutating it mutates the fact for every later listener.
